questions.contextText:
Reading Comprehension (Q.46 – Q.50): Read the following passage carefully and answer the
questions that follow.
Urban heat islands occur when dense concentrations of concrete, asphalt, and glass absorb solar
radiation during the day and release it slowly at night, keeping city temperatures several degrees
warmer than surrounding rural areas. This phenomenon not only escalates peak electricity demand
for air conditioning but also exacerbates heat-related illnesses among outdoor workers and
vulnerable populations. Urban planners increasingly advocate 'blue-green infrastructure'—a
network of shaded street corridors, permeable pavements, rooftop gardens, and restored urban
lakes—to cool neighbourhoods naturally. Unlike mechanical cooling, which shifts heat outdoors and
consumes energy, nature-based solutions address the root cause of urban thermal stress.
questions.questionText: What primarily causes the urban heat island effect?
options: Heat absorption and slow release by concrete and asphalt surfaces
